title: Bow-tie: catastrophic loss of the customer payment rail
caption: Fragility-antifragility audit of the checkout payment pipeline. Center = top event; left = threat pathways with preventive barriers; right = consequences with mitigative barriers. Effectiveness H/M/L per barrier.

hazard_event.label: Checkout payment rail unavailable
hazard_event.description: The top event: customers cannot complete a purchase because the payment-authorization pipeline is down or rejecting all transactions.

threats.label: Primary payment processor outage
threats.pathway: Sole-provider dependency on Stripe authorization API

threats.label: Expired TLS / API credential
threats.pathway: Unrotated secret blocks all auth calls at expiry

threats.label: Fraud-rule misconfiguration declines all cards
threats.pathway: Over-broad risk rule deployed to production rejects legitimate traffic

mitigative_controls.label: Deferred-capture queue replays orders on recovery
Goodwill credit + retry-email to abandoned carts

semantic_description.level_1_elemental: Bow-tie risk diagram. Center red knot is the top event 'Checkout payment rail unavailable'. Three threat nodes on the left, each linked to the knot through preventive barrier bars; three consequence nodes on the right, each linked from the knot through mitigative barrier bars. Barriers are typed (eliminate/reduce/detect on left; reduce/recover/contain on right) and tagged H/M/L effectiveness.
semantic_description.level_2_statistical: 3 threats, 3 consequences, 11 barriers total (6 preventive, 5 mitigative). Preventive effectiveness skews high (3 H, 2 M, 1 reduce-M); mitigative side is weaker on revenue (C1 has only M and L barriers). One escalation factor degrades the highest-rated preventive barrier PC2.
semantic_description.level_3_perceptual: Roughly symmetric left-right structure, but the revenue consequence (C1) is the thin spot: its strongest mitigation is only medium and depends on post-incident replay, so residual risk concentrates on the consequence side even though threats are well-controlled. The failover barrier's hidden DNS dependency is the single point that could collapse the left-side defenses.
semantic_description.level_4_contextual: Fragility audit reading: the system is robust against initiating threats but fragile in consequence recovery for revenue, and the escalation factor reveals correlated failure (failover and DNS share a provider). Antifragile move: decouple DNS and add an independent capture path.
semantic_description.short_alt: Bow-tie: payment-rail outage as center event, 3 threats with preventive barriers left, 3 consequences with mitigative barriers right.
